title: Dock, retain and cycle a DN100 powder-transfer split valve
instruction: Dock and mechanically prove the DN100 powder-transfer split-valve fixture. Align the supported 8 kg upper assembly at X=Y=0, interface height Z=1.000 m, with both discs closed. Turn the retaining collar to 30 degrees, pass the two-second 100 N net separation proof, then turn proof off. Open the active disc to 90 degrees so actual face contact opens the passive disc too. Close both discs, return the collar to zero and raise the upper half to Z=1.100 m. Leave both detached discs seated closed. Do not open an undocked or unlocked half. This is a mechanical readiness test; it does not certify containment.
context: An empty powder-vessel docking interface needs mechanical checkout before battery-ingredient transfers. This dry fixture tests full-size locking, load retention, coupled opening and safe separation; filled-container handling, powder flow and containment certification are excluded.
setup: One fixed dry mechanical layout, SI units. A floor-anchored 100 kg steel guide frame supports a fixed DN100 lower valve at Z=1.000 m and two 2 kg lateral carriages. The upper Z payload totals 8 kg: 7.675 kg vessel/neck/housing/lugs, a 0.125 kg passive steel disc and eight 0.025 kg seal units (3 g radial guide, 2 g tangential guide and 20 g shoe each). Upper initial interface XYZ=(0.008,-0.006,1.100) m. Each complementary disc has radius 50 mm and thickness 2 mm; both pivot about Y and start closed. The active disc is driven; the passive disc has only a 0.5 Nm/rad return spring. Upper housing bore/OD=112/120 mm; lower housing bore/OD=112/160 mm. Three upper lugs centred at radius 70 mm are 24x8x6 mm; a 1 kg aluminium rotating collar with steel retaining inserts has ID200/OD220 mm outer rim, an ID166/OD210 mm bridge and 20-degree slots and three retaining ledges, with 0.1 mm initial vertical lug clearance when docked. Collar and discs start at zero degrees. Actual rotor pins and collar block inhibit opening while unlocked and unlocking while open. Each half has eight 45-degree spring-backed radial seal shoes, ID99.6/OD104 mm, 2 mm axial height, 10 kN/m radial spring and 32 Ns/m radial damping each, contacting its own 100 mm disc with 0.2 mm nominal radial interference. Lateral drives 1.5 MN/m, 10 kNs/m, 1 kN cap, 20 mm/s; vertical force servo 100 kN/m, 1 kNs/m, 1 kN cap, 25 mm/s, disabled during proof. Collar/active drives have 120/600 Nm/rad stiffness, 2 Nms/rad damping, 5/10 Nm caps, and 20/30 deg/s speed limits. Contact friction 0.30 static/0.20 dynamic. Two native RGB cameras and actual encoder/filtered contact instruments. Gravity 9.81 m/s2; native discrete physics 240 Hz, controls 20 Hz. The active disc is 0.125 kg steel. The upper body combines steel valve/lugs and an aluminium vessel/support; its prescribed aggregate mass is 7.675 kg. Each seal carrier is 0.025 kg steel with a reduced spring contact representation of the seating material, not a continuum rubber model. The base and X/Y carriages are steel. The collar interlock can hold an open rotor before the retaining slots clear; positive lug overlap is required whenever a disc is open. The two rotor interlock pins are 4 mm cubes at local (40,125,2) and (0,125,40) mm; the rotating block is 60x18x6 mm centred at (40,125,-3.1) mm. Below-interface supports connect the block to the collar without crossing the rotor sweep. Each solid disc is one closed 32-sided convex mesh with 64 vertices, with maximum radial faceting error 0.25 mm. Each seal shoe has four matching sector colliders; annular housings use 48 sectors. Seal readings are the outward radial component of native disc-contact force. Retaining contact is the downward Z component of collar contact on the upper body; axial/lateral contact cannot count as radial seating. The 112 mm housing bores clear the seal carriers over their full 3 mm outward stroke; the DN100 operating aperture remains defined by the 100 mm discs and their seating shoes. Each 20 g seating shoe has an additional native axial flexure: 1 kN/m spring, 9 Ns/m damping, +/-8 mm stroke and 10 N effort cap, approximating axial lip deformation during opening. Its 3 g radial guide has explicit nonzero inertia. Each guide/shoe assembly remains 25 g, preserving the specified 8 kg upper payload. The eight shoe sectors on each half are centred at 22.5+45*i degrees. Their boundaries coincide with the rotor Y axis, allowing opposite sides of the reduced lip model to deflect in opposite axial directions. No rigid shoe bridges that bending axis. Native full-cycle validation remains required. The current commissioning experiment resolves articulation contacts last in TGS. Private traces include actual native link poses (xyzw quaternion convention, verified against the rotary encoders), processed commands, explicit numeric-order seat joint deflections, total and disc-filtered shoe contacts, and available actuator diagnostic values. Only the documented practical encoders/gauges and RGB reach the policy. The earlier full cycle jammed; no successful demo is claimed. The detailed native camera looks down the open vessel/neck bore from (0,-0.065,1.600) m toward (0,0,1.000), with 55 mm focal length. This exposes actual disc motion without hiding or cutting away colliders. The overview camera is unchanged. Camera visibility still needs inspection in fresh native recordings. Each shoe also has a native tangential flexure: 1 kN/m stiffness, 9 Ns/m damping, +/-2 mm travel, 5 N effort cap and 0.1 m/s speed cap. Guide masses are 3 g radial and 2 g tangential, with a 20 g shoe; the upper total remains 8 kg. The 112 mm housing bores clear combined 3 mm radial and 2 mm tangential travel. TGS requests 64 position iterations and one velocity iteration. This three-axis spring model needs fresh native full-cycle validation. The active-disc drive is now capped at 10 Nm; the collar remains capped at 5 Nm. This is a fixture actuator choice, within the documented 10 Nm theoretical output of a Festo DRVS-32 quarter-turn drive at 6 bar, not an OEM GEA torque curve or a pneumatic-actuator digital twin. The native position servo remains 600 Nm/rad and 2 Nms/rad, with 30 deg/s speed limit. Native contact penetration and the complete cycle require fresh validation. The fixture uses an empty supported upper vessel for dry mechanical commissioning; filled-container transfer and powder containment are outside the task.
scoring: 0.25 for stationary docking within 0.5 mm radial/axial, both discs within 2 degrees closed and all sixteen disc-specific radial contact forces >=0.5 N. 0.5 while docked/locked (collar 27..32 degrees), after two continuous seconds of actual 100+/-1 N net upward proof, downward collar-lug contact >=80 N, one-second encoder ranges <=0.1 mm per linear axis and <=0.5 degree per angle, and displacement from the loaded baseline <=0.1 mm /0.5 degree throughout the hold. 1.0 after that proof, both discs reaching >=88 degrees with <=2 degree disagreement while locked, both reseating closed, and final undocking to Z>=1.095 m with collar within 2 degrees of zero, both discs radially seated and stationary, proof off. Actual opening beyond 2 degrees while undocked or collar below 10 degrees, nonfinite readings or leaving the specified workspace latches zero. Outcome history is measured from native encoders and contact sensors; command values alone cannot earn a score. Stationary means the last full second of encoder samples spans at most 0.1 mm on each linear axis and 0.5 degree on each angular axis. The same criterion applies to partial docking and final detachment. Actual proof effort must be off before crediting the opening and final state. Losing load or retention while proof remains requested erases that proof history.
run_limit: 30 LLM calls; at most 1600 control actions (80 simulated seconds at 20 Hz). A call may select 1..400 actions in explicit waypoints.
reset_notes: Reinitialize joints, velocities and proof history to the stated layout. No powder or consumable is simulated. In a real test use a guarded, supported and empty surrogate vessel; this procedure does not certify hazardous-powder containment.
fidelity: Custom DN100 dry service fixture, 8 kg payload, native collar/interlock contacts and 100 N net free-Z proof. Coupled 100 mm discs close on spring-backed three-axis seats (10 kN/m radial, 1 kN/m axial/tangential), not continuum rubber. Rigid 32-sided discs and 48-sector housings at 240 Hz; ideal guided drives. Powder, leakage, wear and containment certification excluded. Full-cycle native validation pending.
scores: Native model/demo validation pending; not submitted.
